group: LEO allocations quoted at a rounded or combined figure
why: Real allocations to the Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity (a STATE AGENCY receiving RHTP money as a subrecipient, not the grantor), IN the file since session 64 at MDHHS's own grain, and carried by RCJ at a coarser one (§6.1 mode 4): 'Michigan High-Speed Internet Office' $9,100,000 from 'MI - 2026 - September 2026 RHTP Newsletter'; 'Office of Rural Prosperity' $16,700,000 from 'MI - 2026 - Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Visits Michigan to Explore RHT in Action'. MDHHS's roster prices LEO's High Speed Internet Office at $9,104,425 and its Office of Rural Prosperity at $16,130,623 + $600,000 -- RCJ's Rural Prosperity figure is those rows summed and rounded, so neither RCJ row matches a file row on (name, amount) and neither is counted as in the file. An interagency allocation; never a hospital dollar.

group: State Of Michigan RHTP Budget Narrative line items
why: Genuinely RHTP and one tier too high (§0.2, Oklahoma's defect). These are planning figures out of Michigan's own RHTP Budget Narrative, not award actions. Four of the nine names do later appear on the roster as real awardees AT DIFFERENT AMOUNTS -- Berrien County Health Department is $150,000 in the narrative and holds $150,000 + $100,000 on the roster -- and five appear nowhere on it at all, including 'Northern Michigan Center for Rural Health (Technical Assistance for Hubs)' and 'Thumb Alliance - Sanilac County Health Department', which are project labels rather than the recipient names MDHHS awarded under.
disqualifying_evidence: budget-narrative planning figures, not award actions

group: MDHHS community violence intervention grants -- urban, not RHTP
why: MDHHS's 2026-09-21 release awards '$1.5 million to five organizations' for firearm-violence intervention in Flint, Lansing, Saginaw, Benton Harbor and Detroit, $300,000 each for 2026-09-01 to 2028-09-30. The words 'Rural Health Transformation', 'RHTP' and 'rural' occur ZERO times in it. RCJ files four of the five as Michigan RHTP Tier 3 candidates (§0.1 mode 1, wrong programme) -- the successor to the opioid-settlement release whose eight rows RCJ withdrew on this pull.
disqualifying_evidence: "has awarded $1.5 million to five organizations through a competitive grant process"

group: University of Michigan Injury Prevention Center -- Suicide Prevention Council
why: The Michigan Suicide Prevention Council Report's own funding table: 'The State of Michigan appropriated $125,000 in funding to establish the Michigan Suicide Prevention Council', of which $100,000 is a line, and it thanks the University of Michigan Injury Prevention Center for project management. disqualifying_evidence: "The State of Michigan appropriated $125,000 in funding"
